title: Next.js: start from zero
summary: Build a small shop, then find the same ideas in L’ecomax.

lessons.title: 1. Understand your site
lessons.concept: Your site combines a screen, server code and a database.

explanation.text: Think of a shop: the window is the interface, the assistant is the server, the stockroom is the database. Next.js organizes pages and the server. React builds what you see. TypeScript helps catch incorrect value types.

exercise.task: Open the three files below. Find a heading in the page and GET in the API route.
hints: Your site combines a screen, server code and a database.
exercise.solution: page.tsx describes a page. route.ts answers a request. Supabase stores products.

summary: page.tsx describes a page. route.ts answers a request. Supabase stores products.

lessons.title: 2. Set up your workspace
lessons.concept: The terminal runs commands; the editor changes files; the browser shows the result.

explanation.text: Install Node.js and dependencies with npm.cmd ci if missing. A .env.local file configures connections; keep its values private. A network error reaching Supabase can prevent data loading even when Next.js starts.

exercise.task: In a local working copy, open a terminal at the root containing package.json. Run npm.cmd run dev on Windows, then open localhost:3000.
hints: The terminal runs commands; the editor changes files; the browser shows the result.
exercise.solution: The terminal shows Ready and a local address. Keep it open. If the port is busy, use the displayed address.

summary: The terminal shows Ready and a local address. Keep it open. If the port is busy, use the displayed address.

lessons.title: 4. Variables and objects
lessons.concept: A variable names a value. An object groups information about a product.

explanation.text: name is text (string), price is a number. product.price reads an object property. const prevents reassignment of the variable; it does not make every property immutable.

exercise.task: Replace the test page with this example. Change the price to 249 and predict the result before saving.
hints: A variable names a value. An object groups information about a product.
exercise.solution: The page displays Veste: 249 MAD. Curly braces insert a value into JSX.

lessons.title: 5. Reuse a component
lessons.concept: A component is a reusable piece of screen. Props are the values you pass to it.

explanation.text: The type { name: string } says name must be text. className adds styles; border and p-4 are Tailwind classes already used by this site. React component names start with an uppercase letter.

exercise.task: Use this example in the test page. Add a third card with a different name.
hints: A component is a reusable piece of screen. Props are the values you pass to it.
exercise.solution: One function renders several different cards. Changing its class changes all cards.

summary: One function renders several different cards. Changing its class changes all cards.

lessons.title: 6. Make a button respond
lessons.concept: useState keeps a value for the screen. Its setter asks React to update the display.

explanation.text: 'use client' creates a boundary for interactive code. onClick receives a function, not the result of calling it. setCount(value => value + 1) calculates the next value from the previous one. Keep secret keys in server code.

exercise.task: Replace your test page with this counter. Click three times, then reload the page.
hints: useState keeps a value for the screen. Its setter asks React to update the display.
exercise.solution: You see 3, then 0 after reloading. This state lives in the component; it is not saved in a database.

summary: You see 3, then 0 after reloading. This state lives in the component; it is not saved in a database.

teaching.what: useState keeps a value for the screen. Its setter asks React to update the display.
teaching.where: Standalone workshop. This example is not a feature running in L’ECOMAX. Compare the idea with project files in the explorer.

lessons.title: 9. Trace the real flow in L’ecomax
lessons.concept: To understand a feature, follow its data from the source to its display.

explanation.text: The browser must never choose an order’s final price. The server checks prices, stock, sessions and permissions. A service_role key stays server-side. Guide 02 covers tables and RLS; guide 03 covers deployment.

exercise.task: Open /api/products?active=true&limit=3 on your local site. Compare name and price with a product card. In the files, look for PUBLIC_FIELDS and then product.price.
hints: To understand a feature, follow its data from the source to its display.
exercise.solution: You can explain: products table → GET route → JSON → component → screen. Some pages also read data directly on the server.

lessons.title: 10. Work like a developer
lessons.concept: A small verified change is easier to understand and fix.

explanation.text: Continue in this order: APIs → database → deployment → Python if you want an extra service. Then practice forms, accessibility, testing, authentication and performance in the Academy. Your final project: a product list with search, loading, error handling and a test that you can explain without copying.

codeExample.code:
git diff
npx.cmd tsc --noEmit
npm.cmd test

exercise.task: In your working copy, change one text. Read git diff, check phone and desktop layouts, then run the TypeScript check and relevant tests.
hints: A small verified change is easier to understand and fix.
exercise.solution: You can explain what changed, why and how you checked it. If an error occurs, read the first message before changing anything else.
